chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Instrumentation of Toots Johnson's band
summary: The band had banjo, tenor sax, trombone, trumpet (Dimes, Buddy Petit), clarinet, drums and sometimes string bass; no guitars.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Some of the musicians I've interviewed, the old-timers, said that when they played a dance where it was, you know, a normal element of the townspeople, they'd take a violin along to play the leads...
If they had a violin... Toots used to have a violin once in a while. All of them at one time...
I don't mean who played in it (well, we'll get to that later), but what was the instrumentation of Toots Johnson's band, if you remember?
Well, he had a banjo. He had a guy who played a tenor saxophone, a crippled...
...trombone player named Tram... He had different trumpet players. He had a real good trumpet player from New Orleans named Dimes.
Yes. Dimes played with him, and so did Buddy Petit. That's how I happened to play with him sometimes, on account of my teacher.
So in other words, you had a trumpet, a clarinet, a tenor, a trombone, a banjo and a drummer. What about bass? Did they have a bass?
Sometimes. Very seldom, though. More or less in those days it was string bass. But you'd see a lot
I'm thinking now. If you were only 12 years old, this was quite early. Most of the New Orleans bands featured a guitar. I don't want to put words in your mouth...
They had guitars, too. But the bands that I'm talking about...
But Toots Johnson, for instance, played banjo, not guitar.
That's right. And they had a couple of other good banjo players in Baton Rouge. In fact, I can't remember a good guitar player in those bands. All of them were banjo players, to tell you the truth.
